title_short: Valerie Stewart · AYH · Find a Way to Give Back
headline: A housing manager who sees what families coming out of shelters need first says she is happy because she gets to give back, and asks everyone else to do the same.
story: Valerie runs a housing program at RS Eden for parents leaving homelessness. The first thing those families ask her for is shoes, hats, gloves and a coat.

She has been part of the Soles4Souls partnership for years and calls it the most amazing thing they could offer. Asked if she is happy, she says absolutely: this event brings smiles to children in every community.
Her one message to the world is the button: find a way to give back.

[01:05] My name is Valerie Stewart. I'm a housing program manager for RSEden. Excellent. Thank you, Valerie. What is this event and who is it? The event is serving children who are in needed shoes and that comes from all walks of life.
[01:34] The event is going to be Soul for Soul Shoes. I don't know why they've chosen them all over America, but I think it's a great place to have it where they offer the tickets to go into the park after they have gotten here for the shoe event.
[02:01] And I think that's a great, a great, great thing. A new pair of shoes changed for a kid. The fact that if they had shoes that had holes in them or were scuffed up real bad, a new pair of shoes would do a great deal for them.
[02:29] How would they do a great deal for them? They were as if their parents were not able to buy them new shoes for the school year and all their friends came to school that day with new shoes on.
[02:42] They could now be like, oh, I got my new shoes now. So, yeah. So it's kind of a self-esteem or something? Yes, absolutely. It's a self-esteem for the children to, yeah.
[03:01] I'd like to talk to them. I was sitting at the first of the school year, like the first day back, but they do have a pair now. How big of a deal this is? This is a big deal.
[03:22] As I was sitting at the registration office, the desk and the children who got shoes, and they opened up the box, and they were just so happy to show everyone the shoes they received in the shoe event.
[03:36] It was a big deal to them. What I would like for them to take away from this event today is that someone thought was there to give to them, to make them build their self-esteem and go back to school with some new shoes, and knowing that someone do care for you.
[04:10] And there's people out here that was willing to help. The partnership to solve it, I think, is awesome. I heard about it probably about five years ago, and I've been a part of it since, and I just think it's the most amazing thing they could offer.
[04:38] Excellent. Let's go into the volunteer questions here. So, Valerie, why don't you want to be a part of this? The reason why I wanted to be a part of this is to actually see the smile on the kids' face when they got their shoes.
[04:52] And just to say I was a part of it to help bring that smile to their face. How did I hear about it? How did I hear about it? Through my organization, I heard about So4So, so I reached out to the partners and was hoping that they got back in contact with me, and sure enough, they did.

So my organization is RS Eden, and we are a housing program for parents transferring from homelessness, coming from a shelter, coming with little or nothing.
[05:41] And the one thing they always ask me about is shoes, hats, gloves, and a coat. And so I say I can work on a coat and hat, but I definitely know something about the shoes right now.

== 030_3165.MXF (Valerie Stewart) ==
*"Are You Happy?" answers. Length 0:55.*
[00:00] So we're talking to Valerie, are you happy? No, am I happy? Absolutely, I'm happy. I'm happy to be a part of an event that would bring so many smiles and enjoyment to the children in the community, in every community.
[00:31] One message I would get to the entire world is to find a way to give back. Find something, some organization that you can get involved in, or an event that you can help volunteer or seek information to help give back to everyone.
